conviction_note: Wealthfront publishes monthly asset metrics for the first two months of each quarter, so May and June assets are public; building revenue bottom-up from those assets at the company's own last-reported take rates (0.58% cash, 0.21% advisory) lands at roughly $92-94m against a ~$98m consensus, and consensus EPS of $0.13-0.14 still implies a doubling off Q1's $0.07 that no published datapoint supports — sized at -7.5 rather than nearer the 14.35% historical median because this is a model rather than a leak, part of the bad news was already taken when the stock hit $7.20, and the August metrics released tonight will probably carry a positive $100bn headline.

findings.finding: Building Q2 FY27 revenue bottom-up from Wealthfront's own published monthly assets (May: cash $45.0bn / advisory $54.0bn; June: cash $44.8bn / advisory $54.3bn) at the company's own last-reported annualised take rates (cash 0.58%, advisory 0.21%) gives ~$94.5m even assuming July was flat with June, versus a sell-side consensus near $98.0m and an FY27 consensus of $384.9m that requires ~$98m in each remaining quarter.
findings.why_not_priced: The monthly metrics publish ASSETS, not revenue, and the mapping from assets to revenue runs through a take rate that has fallen in consecutive quarters (cash 0.61%->0.58%, advisory 0.22%->0.21%). If the street had done this arithmetic the FY27 revenue line would sit near $370m, not $384.9m, and Q2 EPS consensus would sit near $0.07-0.08 rather than $0.13-0.14 — a sequential doubling off Q1's $0.07 actual. Instead every published price target ($10.50 KBW, $10.50 Goldman, $12.25-$12.42 mean) is still above the $9.655 spot and the consensus rating is Buy with 4 of 6 buys. The price fell to $7.20 and recovered to $9.66; the estimates never made the round trip.
findings.independence: WallStreetZen's FY27 consensus of $384.9m revenue / $0.42 EPS is a second, independently-sourced route to the same gap: https://www.wallstreetzen.com/stocks/us/nasdaq/wlth/stock-forecast (read live 2026-09-09). The May/June asset levels the build rests on come from a different document than the take rates: https://www.globenewswire.com/news-release/2026/07/07/3323635/0/en/wealthfront-reports-june-2026-monthly-metrics.html (2026-07-07).

findings.finding: The mechanical driver of the cash take-rate compression — the 'Direct Deposit Plus' 25bp permanent APY uplift — launched 2026-03-02, so it was live for two of the three months of Q1 FY27 (when the cash rate fell 0.61%->0.58%) and for all three months of Q2 FY27, against a disclosed asset-weighted cross-product adoption of over 63% at June-end and rising.
findings.source_date: read live 2026-09-09; page states base 3.30% APY effective 01/30/2026 and Direct Deposit Plus +0.25% starting March 2, 2026
findings.why_not_priced: This is a full extra month of a permanent giveback on a $45bn book plus a growing adopter base, and it compounds rather than annualises away. If it were in numbers, the sell-side cash take rate for Q2 would be modelled below 0.58% and the revenue consensus would already be below my flat-rate $94.5m case; it is instead $3.5m above it. Note this is a residual on top of finding 1, not a separate quarter.
findings.independence: SHARED SOURCE CLUSTER with finding 1 — the Q1 FY27 earnings release (https://www.sec.gov/Archives/edgar/data/1524566/000162828026040793/q127earningsrelease.htm, 2026-06-04) is where both the 0.61%->0.58% step-down and the incentive's launch are disclosed. Score this as residual only. Independent corroboration that the incentive is still running unchanged and the base APY has not been raised to offset it: https://www.wealthfront.com/cash (read live 2026-09-09, base 3.30% 'as of 01/30/2026').

findings.finding: This stock's reaction function is net deposits, not EPS — the 2026-01-12 print BEAT EPS ($0.21 vs $0.20) and the stock still fell 16.8% on a $208m net deposit outflow against $874m of prior-year inflows — and cash net deposits swung from +$104m in May to -$235m in June while Wealthfront's base APY has been frozen at 3.30% since 2026-01-30 against best-in-market rates now quoted at 4.15-4.21% and Marcus at 3.50% with no strings; July and August flows are both released tonight.
findings.source_date: 2026-03-20 (page-stated); cites 2026-01-12 close $12.59, 2026-01-13 close $10.47, $208m outflow vs $874m prior-year inflow
findings.why_not_priced: The market's last flow datapoint is June, published 2026-07-07; July is the quarter-end month Wealthfront deliberately withholds until the print, and August is released with it, so two consecutive months of the single metric that has moved this stock most are unobserved. The competitive gap that drives them widened through both months — the base APY has not moved in seven months while the Fed held at 3.50-3.75% with three dissenters wanting a hike and long yields broke above 5%. If the market had marked this, a 3.30% payer losing cash would not have rallied 8.97% in five sessions with no company-specific news at all between 2026-08-25 and 2026-09-09.
findings.independence: Different source, same direction — the June flow deterioration itself: https://www.globenewswire.com/news-release/2026/07/07/3323635/0/en/wealthfront-reports-june-2026-monthly-metrics.html (2026-07-07, cash net deposits -$235m, cash assets -2.1% YoY). Competitive rate levels from a third source: https://www.nerdwallet.com/banking/best/high-yield-online-savings-accounts (read live 2026-09-09, 'up to 4.21%').

findings.finding: Tonight's release also carries August 2026 monthly metrics, and with the S&P 500 up 2.7% and the Nasdaq up ~4% in August, Wealthfront's $54.3bn advisory book plus ~$0.4bn of monthly advisory net deposits most likely pushes Total Platform Assets above $100bn for the first time — a round-number headline the company gets to lead with even if the July quarter-end figure is flat-to-down.
findings.source_date: 2026-09 (page covers August 2026; states S&P 500 +2.7% in August after negative June and July)
findings.why_not_priced: The August metric does not exist publicly until tonight — it is not in any aggregator, and Wealthfront's disclosure policy only publishes the first two months of a fiscal quarter in advance, so August (month one of Q3 FY27) arrives bundled with the print. A $100bn milestone is exactly the kind of headline that gets into the first paragraph of the release and blunts a soft quarter. This is the honest offset to my negative findings, and it is why I am not sizing the whole hunt near the 14.35% historical median.
findings.independence: The advisory base and monthly advisory net deposit run-rate come from a different document: https://www.globenewswire.com/news-release/2026/07/07/3323635/0/en/wealthfront-reports-june-2026-monthly-metrics.html (2026-07-07, advisory $54.3bn, advisory net deposits +$399m).

The CEO home-lending related-party overhang as a live risk — it appears cured: the company agreed on 2026-02-16 to buy David Fortunato's entire 95.1% interest in Wealthfront Holdings LLC for nominal consideration, so the January conflict is resolved and the securities investigations are look-back claims, not a fresh catalyst
Any Q2 pre-announcement, guidance or 8-K since the 2026-06-24 Item 5.07 — the company gives no forward guidance at all, which is itself why consensus has been free to drift
baseline_tension: There is no option chain and therefore no skew, so the baseline makes no directional statement at all and its 14.35% 'expected move' is just the median of three reactions that were all negative — my read agrees with that 0/3 history, which is the part most likely already reflected, but it cuts hard against the +8.97% five-day run-up into the print on zero company news and against a Buy consensus whose every price target sits above spot; with nothing priced to beat, my confidence in the magnitude is materially lower than the direction.
